cards.statement: Tailwind generates CSS for the utility classes it finds in your project when you compile your CSS.
cards.explanation: Tailwind isn't one big prebuilt stylesheet: it builds just the styles your classes need at compile time, which is how a one-off class like bg-[#316ff6] works.

cards.statement: Tailwind duplicates the p-4 CSS rule when two elements use p-4.
cards.explanation: Tailwind reuses utility rules across elements.
cards.misconception: Repeated markup duplicates utility CSS.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 retains compatibility with the leading ! utility modifier.
cards.explanation: Tailwind still accepts the older modifier syntax, which is deprecated.

cards.statement: Tailwind composes blur-sm and grayscale through separate CSS variables.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's filter variables combine blur and grayscale.

cards.statement: Tailwind requires shared utility styles to move into a custom CSS class.
cards.explanation: Tailwind documents sharing utility markup through components or template partials.
cards.misconception: Style reuse requires CSS extraction.

cards.statement: A hover utility can read a CSS variable supplied through an inline style.
cards.explanation: The documented pattern uses hover:bg-(--bg-color-hover).

cards.statement: For equally specific, equally important active utilities, later class-attribute order decides the winner.
cards.explanation: For comparable utilities, Tailwind's stylesheet rule order resolves conflicts.
cards.misconception: Markup class order resolves utility conflicts.

cards.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, bg-red-500! marks its generated declaration !important.
cards.explanation: Tailwind adds !important to that utility's declarations.

cards.statement: The important import option raises Tailwind utility selector specificity.
cards.explanation: The import flag marks the entire utility output !important.
cards.misconception: The import flag strengthens selectors.

cards.statement: With prefix(tw), Tailwind emits color variables such as --tw-color-red-500.
cards.explanation: The prefix also applies to generated theme variable names.

cards.statement: With prefix(tw), Tailwind CSS v4 accepts hover:tw:bg-red-500 as the prefixed hover class.
cards.explanation: Tailwind places the prefix first: tw:hover:bg-red-500.
cards.misconception: A prefix follows state variants.

cards.statement: A :root color variable can register matching Tailwind utilities.
cards.explanation: Utility registration needs @theme, rather than :root.
cards.misconception: Ordinary variables register utility APIs.

cards.statement: A --font-editor theme token can generate a font-weight utility.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's --font-* namespace generates font-family utilities.
cards.misconception: Font tokens configure weight.

cards.statement: Adding --font-script in @theme replaces the default font-family utilities.
cards.explanation: New theme tokens extend the imported defaults.
cards.misconception: Adding a token replaces its namespace.

cards.statement: Redefining --color-red-500 in @theme changes the value used by bg-red-500.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's bg-red-500 reads the redefined --color-red-500 token.

cards.statement: In @theme, --color-*: initial removes default palette utilities.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's color wildcard reset clears the imported palette API.

cards.statement: In @theme, --*: initial removes Tailwind's flex utility.
cards.explanation: Static utilities like flex survive theme resets.
cards.misconception: A theme reset removes static utilities.

cards.statement: With @theme inline, --font-sans: var(--font-inter) makes font-sans reference var(--font-sans).
cards.explanation: Tailwind emits font-family: var(--font-inter) for that utility.
cards.misconception: Inline retains the theme-variable indirection.

cards.statement: Tailwind emits unused theme variables when @theme static defines them.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's static option retains unused theme variables in output.

cards.statement: A CSS @import can share @theme tokens between Tailwind projects.
cards.explanation: Importing the shared stylesheet supplies its theme definitions.

cards.statement: Tailwind finds utility candidates by parsing the class attributes in your HTML templates.
cards.explanation: Tailwind treats every source file as plain text and picks out class-like tokens wherever they appear, without parsing the file as code.
cards.misconception: Tailwind parses HTML class attributes instead of scanning source files as plain text.

cards.statement: Tailwind detects complete class strings selected from a lookup object.
cards.explanation: Complete strings remain visible in scanned source.

cards.statement: Tailwind automatically scans node_modules for utility classes.
cards.explanation: Dependency files need explicit source registration.
cards.misconception: Automatic scanning includes dependencies.

cards.statement: Tailwind excludes CSS files from automatic class detection.
cards.explanation: Tailwind skips CSS sources.

cards.statement: Tailwind resolves @source paths relative to the build's working directory.
cards.explanation: Tailwind resolves @source paths from the stylesheet.
cards.misconception: Explicit sources use the working directory.

cards.statement: With source(none), Tailwind scans paths registered through @source.
cards.explanation: Explicit paths supply sources when automatic detection is disabled.

cards.statement: An @source inline('underline') directive can generate an otherwise undetected utility.
cards.explanation: Tailwind generates valid candidates supplied through @source inline().

cards.statement: An @source inline('underline') directive can also generate hover:underline.
cards.explanation: Variant classes need explicit inline-source entries.
cards.misconception: Safelisting a base class includes variants.

cards.statement: Tailwind expands bg-red-{100..900..100} inside @source inline() into candidate classes.
cards.explanation: Brace ranges supply multiple candidates.

cards.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, hover: includes a media condition for primary-input hover capability.
cards.explanation: Tailwind wraps the :hover rule in (hover: hover).

cards.statement: A focus-within: utility can style a wrapper while its descendant has focus.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's focus-within: rules match focus in the element or its descendants.

cards.statement: Tailwind's disabled: variant matches a button that signals its state with aria-disabled="true" alone.
cards.explanation: disabled: compiles to :disabled, which needs the native disabled state; a button marked only with aria-disabled="true" needs Tailwind's aria-disabled: variant.
cards.misconception: Tailwind's disabled: variant also matches aria-disabled="true".

cards.statement: Tailwind's invalid: styles show on an empty required field before the user has typed anything.
cards.explanation: invalid: compiles to :invalid, which matches as soon as the value fails validation; Tailwind's user-invalid: variant waits until the user has interacted with the field.

cards.statement: Tailwind's checked: variant matches a checkbox through its checked HTML attribute.
cards.explanation: Tailwind generates a :checked condition for live state.
cards.misconception: The variant tests initial attribute presence.

cards.statement: Tailwind's focus:invalid: utilities apply when both form-state conditions match.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's focus:invalid: rules combine :focus and :invalid.

cards.statement: With dark overridden to &:where(.dark, .dark *), Tailwind still requires the system's dark preference.
cards.explanation: With the .dark selector override, Tailwind activates dark: through matching markup.
cards.misconception: Selector dark mode also requires system dark.

cards.statement: With dark set to &:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *), dark: also targets the marked element.
cards.explanation: The documented data-theme dark selector includes the marked element itself.

cards.statement: Tailwind's selector-based dark variant can persist the user's theme choice in localStorage.
cards.explanation: The application owns persistence of theme preferences.
cards.misconception: Tailwind manages saved theme preferences.

cards.statement: Tailwind's group-focus: responds to focus on an ancestor marked group.
cards.explanation: Tailwind targets .group:focus ancestors.

cards.statement: Tailwind's peer-invalid: can style a sibling that appears before the peer marker.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's peer variants target following siblings.
cards.misconception: Peer variants reach earlier siblings.

cards.statement: Tailwind's has-checked: can style an element containing a checked descendant.
cards.explanation: Tailwind generates a :has(:checked) condition.

cards.statement: Tailwind's group-has-[a]: looks for a link inside the styled element's own subtree.
cards.explanation: group-has-[a]: runs its :has() check on the element marked group, so the link can sit anywhere inside that group.
cards.misconception: The styled target supplies the searched subtree.

cards.statement: Tailwind's in-focus: variant reacts to focus on any parent element, whether or not that parent has the group class.
cards.explanation: The in-* variants respond to a state change in any ancestor and need no marker class, so in-focus: also fires when an outer wrapper higher up receives focus.

cards.statement: Tailwind's group-[.is-ready]: searches above the group marker for an .is-ready ancestor.
cards.explanation: group-[.is-ready]: combines .group and .is-ready on one element.
cards.misconception: The arbitrary selector describes another ancestor.

cards.statement: Tailwind's data-active: waits for data-active to equal 'true'.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's data-active: tests attribute presence.
cards.misconception: Data presence variants test boolean values.

cards.statement: Tailwind's aria-expanded: activates when aria-expanded='false'.
cards.explanation: Tailwind matches aria-expanded="true" for aria-expanded:.
cards.misconception: Boolean ARIA variants also match false.

cards.statement: Tailwind's sm: utilities target viewports below the sm threshold.
cards.explanation: Tailwind generates a minimum-width condition for sm:.
cards.misconception: sm: identifies small-screen upper bounds.

cards.statement: Tailwind excludes the md boundary from max-md: rules.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's max-md: uses a strict upper comparison.

cards.statement: Tailwind treats md:xl:flex as the bounded range form of its responsive API.
cards.explanation: Tailwind uses md:max-xl: for a bounded viewport interval.
cards.misconception: Two minimum prefixes define a bounded range.

cards.statement: Tailwind emits default lg: media queries that read --breakpoint-lg through var().
cards.explanation: Tailwind embeds breakpoint lengths directly into media-query conditions.
cards.misconception: Breakpoint conditions read theme variables at runtime.

cards.statement: Setting --breakpoint-2xl: initial in @theme keeps 2xl: available at its original threshold.
cards.explanation: Tailwind removes 2xl: when --breakpoint-2xl is set to initial.
cards.misconception: initial restores the imported breakpoint.

cards.statement: Above lg, equally specific normal md:w-32 and lg:w-48 utilities resolve to lg:w-48 in Tailwind's output.
cards.explanation: Tailwind orders responsive rules by breakpoint size.

cards.statement: Tailwind normalizes mixed px and rem breakpoint tokens before ordering responsive utility rules.
cards.explanation: Mixed breakpoint units can produce unexpected generated ordering.
cards.misconception: Tailwind converts units before sorting.

cards.statement: Tailwind's min-[37rem]: produces a viewport threshold outside the named breakpoint scale.
cards.explanation: Arbitrary variants supply one-off viewport thresholds.

cards.statement: An @theme --breakpoint-tablet token automatically makes max-tablet: available.
cards.explanation: Tailwind generates a maximum variant for a breakpoint.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 routes container variants through a separately installed container-query plugin.
cards.explanation: Container variants belong to Tailwind CSS v4's core.
cards.misconception: Container queries retain their plugin integration.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4.3 uses @container-size for descendant utilities with block-size container units.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's @container-size marker establishes size containment.

cards.statement: Tailwind evaluates @md:flex using the viewport's width.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's @md: variant checks an ancestor container's width.
cards.misconception: Container variants measure the viewport.

cards.statement: Tailwind's @sm: variant stops matching once its container reaches the @md size.
cards.explanation: Tailwind compiles @sm: to @container (width >= 24rem), a minimum with no upper bound, so its styles stay active as the container grows past @md.
cards.misconception: Named container variants represent size bands.

cards.statement: Tailwind's @max-md: threshold tracks changes to --breakpoint-md in @theme.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's @max-md: threshold belongs to the --container-* scale.
cards.misconception: Viewport tokens also set container thresholds.

cards.statement: Tailwind compiles @sm:@max-md: into a bounded container-query interval.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's @sm:@max-md: stack supplies lower and upper thresholds.

cards.statement: Tailwind's @sm/main: selects @container/main beyond a nearer, differently named container.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's named container variant identifies its intended ancestor.

cards.statement: A --container-card token in @theme makes Tailwind's max-w-card utility available.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's --container-* namespace also registers size utilities.

cards.statement: Tailwind accepts container units as arbitrary utility values, such as w-[50cqw].
cards.explanation: Tailwind's width declaration retains the supplied cqw value.

cards.statement: Tailwind inlines a variable's resolved value when compiling w-(--panel-width).
cards.explanation: Tailwind emits width: var(--panel-width) for w-(--panel-width).
cards.misconception: Variable shorthand resolves to a build-time literal.

cards.statement: Tailwind can compile text-(length:--label-size) as color when --label-size contains a color.
cards.explanation: The length: hint selects Tailwind's font-size API.
cards.misconception: Variable values override explicit type hints.

cards.statement: Tailwind decodes underscores in grid-cols-[1fr_2fr] into spaces in the generated value.
cards.explanation: Tailwind emits grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr.

cards.statement: Tailwind decodes the underscore in bg-[url('/team_photo.png')] into a space in its generated URL.
cards.explanation: Tailwind preserves underscores inside URL values.
cards.misconception: Whitespace decoding changes URL filenames.

cards.statement: Tailwind preserves the escaped underscore in before:content-['user\_name'] in the generated content.
cards.explanation: Tailwind keeps an escaped underscore literal in arbitrary values.

cards.statement: Tailwind emits an ordinary CSS custom property from md:[--panel-gap:24px].
cards.explanation: Tailwind's [--panel-gap:24px] generates a CSS variable assignment.

cards.statement: Tailwind substitutes the element carrying a class for & in the arbitrary variant [&.selected]:underline.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's & placeholder identifies the utility's own element.

cards.statement: Tailwind accepts [@supports(display:grid)]:grid with an implicit utility target.
cards.explanation: Arbitrary at-rule variants work with the & placeholder omitted.

cards.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, first:*:pt-0 styles the first child inside the element carrying the class.
cards.explanation: Tailwind applies first: before *:, targeting children of an element that is itself a first child.
cards.misconception: v4 retains right-to-left variant interpretation.

cards.statement: Importing tailwindcss includes Preflight in Tailwind's base layer.
cards.explanation: The default Tailwind import brings in preflight.css under layer(base).

cards.statement: Preflight retains a paragraph's browser-provided vertical margins in Tailwind's base styles.
cards.explanation: Preflight resets paragraph margins to zero.
cards.misconception: Paragraph spacing survives the default reset.

cards.statement: Preflight's border reset strips the browser-drawn borders from text inputs and buttons.
cards.explanation: Preflight applies border: 0 solid to every element plus ::before, ::after, ::backdrop and ::file-selector-button, which overrides the user-agent borders on text inputs and buttons.

cards.statement: Preflight selects Tailwind's text-2xl token as the default font size for h1 headings.
cards.explanation: Preflight makes h1 font size and font weight inherit.
cards.misconception: Preflight assigns headings a default type-scale step.

cards.statement: Preflight preserves browser numbering on ordered lists in Tailwind's base styles.
cards.explanation: Preflight applies list-style: none to ordered lists.
cards.misconception: Ordered lists retain their browser numbering.

cards.statement: Preflight changes images and videos to block display in Tailwind's base styles.
cards.explanation: Preflight includes img and video in its display: block reset.

cards.statement: Preflight stretches a narrow image to its parent's width with a width: 100% declaration.
cards.explanation: Preflight constrains images with max-width: 100% rather than assigning that width.
cards.misconception: The responsive reset expands images to fill their parent.

cards.statement: Tailwind's docs put a project's own element defaults, such as h1 styles, in @layer base rather than @layer components.
cards.explanation: Element defaults belong in Tailwind's base layer, for example @layer base { h1 { color: red; } }; the docs keep @layer components for class-based components like .card.

cards.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, a normal utility beats a conflicting normal @layer components rule with a more specific selector.
cards.explanation: Tailwind orders its utilities layer after components; for declarations without !important a later cascade layer wins whatever the selector specificity.

cards.statement: Preflight selects content-box as the default box-sizing value for its reset targets.
cards.explanation: Preflight sets box-sizing: border-box on its reset targets.
cards.misconception: Preflight preserves the browser's content-box sizing default.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 uses property count as a sorting criterion for custom @utility rules.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's sorting helps utilities with fewer properties override broader custom utilities.

cards.statement: A custom @utility tab-4 definition lets Tailwind generate focus:tab-4.
cards.explanation: Tailwind registers custom utilities with its existing variant API.

cards.statement: Tailwind inserts @utility definitions into its components layer alongside component styles.
cards.explanation: Tailwind inserts custom utilities into the utilities layer.
cards.misconception: Custom utilities use the component layer.

cards.statement: A nested &::-webkit-scrollbar rule inside @utility styles the scrollbar of the element using that utility.
cards.explanation: Nesting inside @utility adds an extra selector to the generated utility, as in the docs' scrollbar-hidden example.

cards.statement: With @theme { --tab-size-team: 8; }, @utility tab-* { tab-size: --value(--tab-size-*); } gives tab-team tab-size: 8.
cards.explanation: Tailwind resolves the team suffix against --tab-size-team.

cards.statement: @utility tabstop-* { tab-size: --value(integer); } accepts tabstop-[8] as a matching utility.
cards.explanation: Tailwind accepts tabstop-[8] when tabstop-* uses --value([integer]).
cards.misconception: A bare-value resolver also accepts bracketed arbitrary values.

cards.statement: Tailwind replaces an unresolved --value() declaration with the property's initial value.
cards.explanation: Tailwind omits declarations whose --value() calls fail to resolve.
cards.misconception: A failed value resolver emits a reset declaration.

cards.statement: For tab-2 with @theme { --tab-size-2: 8; }, Tailwind's --value(--tab-size-*, integer) picks the theme value.
cards.explanation: Tailwind tries --value() arguments in order and uses the first successful match.

cards.statement: Defining @utility shift-* also registers Tailwind's corresponding -shift-* classes.
cards.explanation: Tailwind uses a separate @utility -shift-* definition for the negative form.
cards.misconception: Positive functional definitions register their negative counterparts.

cards.statement: Tailwind joins selectors when @apply reuses an existing utility inside a custom rule.
cards.explanation: Tailwind inserts utility declarations into the rule containing @apply.
cards.misconception: @apply shares rules through selector joining.

cards.statement: Tailwind applies @variant dark to declarations nested inside a custom CSS rule.
cards.explanation: The @variant block wraps those declarations in the chosen Tailwind condition.

cards.statement: Tailwind uses @reference to expose main-stylesheet definitions inside separately processed CSS Modules.
cards.explanation: @reference makes theme variables, custom utilities, and custom variants available to CSS Modules.

cards.statement: In a customized project, @reference 'tailwindcss' exposes app.css custom utilities.
cards.explanation: A customized project's separate stylesheets reference its main stylesheet to see its custom definitions.
cards.misconception: Referencing Tailwind itself includes application customizations.

cards.statement: Tailwind copies referenced stylesheet rules into component output when it processes @reference.
cards.explanation: @reference supplies definitions while omitting the referenced stylesheet's emitted styles.
cards.misconception: Reference imports duplicate the stylesheet's rules.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 starts its stylesheet through @import 'tailwindcss'.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's current entry stylesheet imports the framework using CSS @import.

cards.statement: Tailwind bundles local CSS @import files into the project's compiled stylesheet.
cards.explanation: Tailwind performs CSS import bundling during compilation.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 adds vendor prefixes itself, which makes autoprefixer unnecessary in its PostCSS setup.
cards.explanation: Vendor prefixing is part of Tailwind's own CSS processing in v4, so the upgrade guide removes autoprefixer from the PostCSS plugin list.

cards.statement: Tailwind's docs name the PostCSS plugin as the most seamless way to add Tailwind to SvelteKit.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's docs call the Vite plugin the most seamless way to integrate with frameworks like Laravel, SvelteKit, React Router, Nuxt and SolidJS.
cards.misconception: The PostCSS plugin is the recommended integration for Vite-based frameworks.

cards.statement: Tailwind CLI provides a standalone executable that performs Tailwind compilation outside Node.js.
cards.explanation: The standalone Tailwind CLI executable runs independently of a Node.js installation.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 documents Sass as a supported preprocessing stage in its build workflow.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4's documented workflow is not designed for Sass, Less, or Stylus.
cards.misconception: Tailwind v4 retains a documented Sass preprocessing stage.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 automatically discovers tailwind.config.js during compilation.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 loads a JavaScript configuration when CSS explicitly names it with @config.
cards.misconception: Legacy JavaScript configuration discovery remains automatic.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 gives CSS definitions precedence when legacy configuration values conflict.
cards.explanation: Tailwind merges CSS and legacy configuration where possible; conflicting CSS definitions take precedence.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 honors corePlugins, safelist, and separator in a JavaScript configuration.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 excludes corePlugins, safelist, and separator from supported JavaScript options.
cards.misconception: Legacy JavaScript options retain complete compatibility.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 retains theme() as a deprecated compatibility function.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's theme() function remains available for legacy usage despite its deprecated status.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 exposes resolveConfig for resolving a legacy JavaScript theme.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 removes the resolveConfig function exported by v3.
cards.misconception: resolveConfig remains part of the v4 JavaScript API.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 preserves an untouched to-* stop when a dark:from-* utility changes a gradient.
cards.explanation: Changing a gradient stop through a v4 variant retains the other stop values.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 uses currentColor as the default color for borders and rings.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4's default border and ring colors follow currentColor.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 resets scale-150 when focus:transform-none becomes active.
cards.explanation: Tailwind CSS v4 uses an individual scale property; focus:scale-none resets scale-150.
cards.misconception: transform-none resets utilities backed by individual transform properties.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4's space-y-* selector filters out children carrying a hidden attribute.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's v4 space-y-* selector matches direct children except the last, including hidden children.
cards.misconception: The space selector retains v3's hidden-child filter.

cards.statement: Tailwind CSS v4 puts divide-y-* separators on the bottom edge of preceding children.
cards.explanation: Tailwind's v4 divide-y-* utilities assign bottom borders to direct children except the last.

cards.statement: In Tailwind CSS v4, --container-* tokens in @theme set the container utility's centering and padding.
cards.explanation: The upgrade guide replaces v3's container center and padding options with CSS: @utility container { margin-inline: auto; padding-inline: 2rem; }.
cards.misconception: Container centering and padding moved into --container-* theme tokens.
